workflowTriggers.source.label: Source
workflowTriggers.input.label: Input
workflowTriggers.input.unknown: No input guide is available yet. Refer to the server-provided fields below or this trigger’s description.
workflowTriggers.configure.label: Setup
workflowTriggers.configure.unknown: This interface has no setup guide for this trigger yet. Refer to the server description and available editor controls.
workflowTriggers.manual.label: Run from the workflow page
workflowTriggers.manual.withInput: Supported with supplied input. This executes the activities with real effects; it is not a preview and does not subscribe to an event.
workflowTriggers.manual.configured: Supported using the trigger configuration. This executes the activities with real effects; review the configuration first.
workflowTriggers.manual.unavailable: No generic Run now entry. Start from the corresponding feature, which prepares the required task and input.
workflowTriggers.catalog.description: This directory lists the triggers registered by the current server. Activation mode describes how they normally start; Run now support is a separate capability. System events go to enabled workflows with matching filters. Feature-managed workflows are selected by their owning feature. Passing validation does not guarantee future network, file or account availability.
workflowTriggers.catalog.error: Could not load this server’s triggers. Refresh to try again.
workflowTriggers.catalog.unavailable: This server has not provided details for this trigger.
workflowTriggers.catalog.empty: No registered triggers match this filter.
workflowTriggers.catalog.noFields: The server has not exposed any input fields.
workflowTriggers.guide.postParser.manual: A supported post link or pasted text, with an optional title. Read and extract activities produce structured download clues.
Configure read and extract activities, and an AI provider when using AI extraction. Supply input on the workflow page or create a saved task in Post parser.
workflowTriggers.guide.acquisition.reque: The resource, selected acquisition link and owned acquisition task, prepared by Acquire resources.

Add a supported link in Acquire resources and select a workflow. Configure accounts, download settings and directories required by its activities. Enabling a workflow does not make it handle every acquisition task.
workflowTriggers.guide.downloader.result: A saved downloader result, including its path, result kind and original task. Torrent files and direct content can use different follow-up handling.
Bind a workflow under Download result follow-up in downloader settings and configure accepted result kinds. Only the workflow bound to that task is started; task completion is a separate trigger.
workflowTriggers.guide.subscription.upda: Resources newly added to the collection by a subscription check, with subscription and source information. Initial baseline setup does not publish this event.
Configure a subscription, then create and enable a workflow with this trigger. Optionally filter subscriptions and sources. Later checks trigger it only when matching new resources are found.
workflowTriggers.guide.downloader.comple: One completed downloader task with source, name and task details; not one item per file.

Choose downloader-source filters and enable the workflow, for example for completion notifications. To handle torrent or archive files, use Download result ready and bind the workflow in downloader settings.
workflowTriggers.guide.acquisition.statu: The acquisition task, associated resource and new status. Task creation also produces a status update.
Select the statuses to react to and enable the workflow, for example to notify on failure or completion. It reacts to progress; it does not select or start acquisition workflows.
workflowTriggers.guide.collection.member: Resources newly added to a collection and how they were added (manually or by subscription). Existing members are not emitted again.

Filter collections and membership origins, then enable the workflow. Removal, reordering and re-adding existing resources do not trigger it. A resource dynamically matching collection filters is not a membership-add event.
workflowTriggers.guide.resource.material: A resource successfully linked to local content, with its source. General resource creation and arbitrary file changes are not this event.
Filter resource sources and enable the workflow. It fires after the materialization process successfully links local content; unlinking does not trigger it.
workflowTriggers.guide.fs.manualScan.inp: Server files or directories selected by root folders, depth, target kind and extension filters.
workflowTriggers.guide.fs.manualScan.con: Choose existing directories accessible to the server and configure the scan range, then run manually. No timer or directory event starts this trigger automatically.
Files or directories found in each scan of the configured server folders, not only entries added since the previous run.
Configure the scan range and interval in minutes, then enable the workflow. An interval below one minute disables scheduling; manual runs remain available. Check run history for actual execution.
workflowTriggers.guide.fs.watch.input: Direct child entries created, changed or renamed in watched directories, after no further changes are observed for the settle period.
workflowTriggers.guide.fs.watch.configur: Configure existing server directories, target kind, extensions and settle time, then enable. Existing content is not scanned initially and subfolders are not watched recursively. Settling reduces the risk of processing an unfinished file; it does not prove a download has completed.
workflow.trigger.postParserManual.descri: Run manually with one supported post link or pasted text. Saved post-parser tasks start their own linked run from the post parser. This is not a broadcast subscription and parsing alone creates no resource or download task.
workflow.trigger.acquisitionRequested.de: Start this workflow from Acquire resources with a resource, acquisition link and owned task. It runs only the selected recipe; enabling another recipe does not subscribe it to every acquisition.
workflow.trigger.downloaderResultReady.d: After a downloader saves a result, it starts the follow-up workflow configured for that task. It processes the saved result, does not broadcast to all workflows using this trigger, and is separate from overall task completion.
workflow.trigger.subscriptionUpdated.des: After a subscription check adds new resources to its collection, enabled workflows whose subscription and source filters match receive those resources. The first initialization and checks with no additions do not publish this event.
workflow.trigger.downloaderCompleted.des: When a downloader task completes, enabled workflows matching its downloader source receive the completed task. This includes a pre-check that finds nothing left to download. It is one event per completed task, not per downloaded file or saved result.
workflow.trigger.acquisitionStatusChange: When an acquisition task is created or its state changes, enabled workflows matching the configured states receive its resource, status and task details. This reacts to progress; it does not choose or start an acquisition recipe.
When resources are newly added to a collection, enabled workflows matching the collection and membership origin receive only the newly added resources. Re-adding existing members, removal and reordering do not publish this event.
workflow.trigger.resourceMaterialized.de: When the materialization service successfully links a resource to existing local content, enabled workflows matching its resource sources receive that resource. This is not an event for every resource creation or filesystem change, and unlinking content does not publish it.
workflow.trigger.fsManualScan.descriptio: Run manually to scan configured existing directories and produce file or directory items. No event or timer starts this trigger; root directories and scan options must be configured first.
workflow.trigger.fsScheduledScan.descrip: Scan configured existing directories on the configured interval, or run manually. An interval below one minute disables automatic scheduling. A queued, running or waiting execution prevents another scheduled run.
workflow.trigger.fsWatch.description: Watch direct children of configured existing directories. Created, modified or renamed entries trigger after they remain quiet for the configured time. Existing entries are not scanned initially and subdirectories are not watched recursively; manual input replays supplied paths.
